text:
alex.supp: customer reporting spikes of 401s and duplicate POSTs after our TS SDK retries kicked in. billing doubled for a few requests. sending logs. :frowning:

customer_john: repro attached — our webhook got the same order created twice, and the client shows two successful responses but server got two POSTs. no idempotency header used.

priya.eng: can you paste the SDK snippet you used? curious whether AbortController is reused across retries.

customer_john: here's the call (simplified):
```ts
const ac = new AbortController()
await client.post('/orders', { body: order }, { signal: ac.signal })
```
We call this inside a retry wrapper that re-throws and re-invokes the whole function.

mike.sre: two quick things — (1) if the SDK retries internally it must create fresh signal per attempt, otherwise abort semantics can leak; (2) duplicate POSTs => recommend idempotency-key header as immediate mitigation.

priya.eng: what Node + undici versions? there are subtle differences in global fetch behavior between node 18/20 and undici versions that affect stream reuse on retry.

customer_john: Node 20.5, undici 5.13.0, ts-sdk 0.9.2

priya.eng: ok that undici version had a known issue where passing the same ReadableStream body across retries produced truncated streams on retry path — SDK shouldn't be retrying non-idempotent requests without explicit opt-in. do you have retry enabled? show config.

customer_john: we rely on SDK defaults. I didn't set retry config.

alex.supp: aha — default retry policy is conservative but we have a bug: abort controller passed from caller gets forwarded to each attempt instead of new internal controller per attempt. that plus undici stream behavior could explain duplicates + transient 401s if token rotation happens between attempts.

priya.eng: quick repro I ran locally:
```ts
// bad pattern: reusing signal across attempts
async function sendOnce(client, body, signal) {
  return client.fetch('/api', { method: 'POST', body, signal })
}

// if fetch throws and caller retries, the same body stream/signal can be in a bad state
```

mike.sre: customer reported 401s interleaved with 200s — likely token refresh race. If retry queue replays after we rotated token but client used old Authorization header, first attempt 401 triggers refresh, second attempt uses new token but if SDK doesn't atomically update header for replay, weird combos happen.

customer_john: logs: server saw 401 for request-id a1, then accepted request-id a2. client logs show both returned 200. I'll attach timestamps.

ci-bot: deploy bot: rolled canary of ts-sdk@0.9.3 to internal testing cluster at 2026-03-16T14:50:00Z

priya.eng: immediate mitigations for you:
- set header "Idempotency-Key" on POSTs
- set SDK option retry: { retries: 0 } until we patch
- avoid passing your AbortController into SDK top-level call; create controllers for higher-level cancellation only

alex.supp: longterm fix: SDK patch will (A) never retry non-idempotent methods by default unless user enables ; (B) clone/derive a fresh AbortController per attempt and not reuse request body streams; (C) ensure per-retry header refresh picks latest auth token.

priya.eng: minimal patch landed in branch fix/retry-signal-2026. tests added for: signal per attempt, idempotency guidance, and token refresh during retry. planning release v0.9.4 tomorrow.

customer_john: thanks — I'll toggle retries off and add idempotency keys for now. can you CC me when 0.9.4 is out? my account was hit with extra invoice already.

alex.supp: cc you when released. sorry for the trouble — we'll fast-track a patch and refund for the duplicated billing event (raised billing ticket #B-8421).

mike.sre: follow-up todo: add an integration test in CI that simulates token rotation during retry window and asserts no duplicate non-idempotent side effects.

priya.eng: also adding a short doc blurb in SDK README about Node/undici stream incompatibilities and recommended patterns (create fresh body or use Buffer for retries).

customer_john: verification steps I used:
1) set Node 20.5 with undici 5.13 (same as prod)
2) run an app that performs POST without idempotency header
3) force auth refresh on quick subsequent requests (we have a dev hook to drop token)
4) observe duplicate resources and mixed 401/200 in client logs

priya.eng: thanks — that repro is super useful. we'll prioritize.

alex.supp: closing loop once 0.9.4 is released and refund processed. :thumbsup:
